# Hmac&lt;D&gt;

An incremental HMAC over any digest.

```rux
pub struct Hmac<D: Digest> {
    // private fields
}
```

`prototype` supplies both the algorithm and its parameters; it is copied rather than consumed, so one
prototype can start any number of authentications.
Structural `Copy` whenever `D` is copyable; copying snapshots both digest states independently.

## Type parameters

| Name        | Description     |
| ----------- | --------------- |
| `D: Digest` | the digest type |

## Constructors

<h3 id="new"><code>Hmac</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Hmac(prototype: D, key: char8[..]) -> Hmac<D>
```

An HMAC keyed with `key`.
A key longer than the digest's block is replaced by its own digest, which is what the specification says
and is worth knowing: two keys differing only past the block length authenticate identically, because
they are the same key after this step. A shorter key is padded with zeros.

| Name        | Type        | Description                                          |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `prototype` | `D`         | any value of the digest type, read only to select it |
| `key`       | `char8[..]` | the key                                              |

**Returns**: an authenticator keyed with those bytes

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Hmac.rux#L50)

## Related

<h3 id="hmac-maximum-block"><code>HmacMaximumBlock</code></h3>

```rux
pub const HmacMaximumBlock: uint = 168;
```

The longest block any supported digest uses, which is what the padded key buffers are sized to.
SHAKE128's rate is the largest at a hundred and sixty eight bytes; SHA-512's block is a hundred and twenty
eight and SHA-256's sixty four. The buffers below are written as that literal because an array length must
be a compile-time integer and a constant does not satisfy that yet.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Hmac.rux#L24)
